data.hook_b: Does your sump overflow? In Hyderabad that's now a *₹1,000* fine
data.tldr: HMWSSB's water emergency moves most of the city from alternate-day supply to once every three days, with fines for wastage.

beats.what: Water Board MD Ashok Reddy declared a water emergency and a restricted supply schedule.
beats.why: Osman Sagar, Himayat Sagar and Singur are low; some may run dry mid to late December.
beats.care: Store water on supply day, fix overflowing tanks now, and book tankers early.

cards.title: 🆕 What the emergency changes
cards.body: Most of Hyderabad moves from alternate-day water to once every three days. Secunderabad Cantonment and the outskirts get water only once every three or four days. The board is adding tankers and starting tanker registration. New borewell permits for construction and other non-drinking uses will be limited.

cards.title: 💸 The fines
cards.body: First-time wasters pay ₹1,000. Homes and resident welfare associations that let tanks or pumps overflow pay more. Repeat offenders risk steeper fines or losing their water and sewer connection under the HMWSSB Act, 1989.

cards.title: 🆕 Tankers up 233% in October
cards.body: HMWSSB logged 62,565 tanker bookings in October, against 18,806 last year. Off-season it normally gets 800–1,500 a day. Demand is about 735 million gallons a day; supply is about 585. Boduppal, LB Nagar and Manikonda lean hardest on tankers.

cards.title: Why now?
cards.body: Osman Sagar holds 2.2 of 3.5 TMC, Himayat Sagar 2.1 of 2.5 TMC, Singur just 3.4 of 29.9 TMC. Only 3 of the city's 16 mandals got enough rain. The city books 6,000–8,000 tankers a day. Critics like M Srinivas of the Urban Development Forum say the steps came too late.

Under the water emergency, how often will most of Hyderabad get piped water?
cards.why: HMWSSB moved most of the city from alternate-day to once-every-three-days supply (Siasat, Oct 25).

learn.t: 1 TMC = 1 thousand million cubic feet, about 28,317 million litres of water.

cards.title: 🆕 Evening update (Oct 27): NDRF 31 teams, 600 km track watched
cards.body: NDRF has deployed 31 teams across states and a UT likely to be hit as very severe Cyclone Arnab nears the Andhra coast near Yanam; shelters are open and fishermen told to stay ashore (NDRF DIG, via Telangana Today). Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw says 600 km of rail track is under close watch ahead of landfall (Indian Express). Still travelling east by train on Oct 28–29? Check NTES before you leave.

cards.title: 🆕 Afternoon update (Oct 27): SCR cancels 12 trains
cards.body: South Central Railway has cancelled 12 trains because of Cyclone Arnab (Deccan Chronicle). Check your train's status on NTES or the SCR site before leaving home. Telangana's IMD alerts are unchanged.

cards.title: 🆕 Midday update (Oct 27): Arnab speeds up, Odisha moves 48,000
cards.body: Arnab was moving at 22 kmph over the past 6 hours, up from 13 kmph in Monday's bulletin. Odisha is evacuating 48,000 people in eight districts; Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh Pravakar Patil said it will hit Malkangiri district after crossing the Andhra–Yanam coast. Andhra's Bapatla district has opened a 24-hour control room with emergency helplines. Jharkhand has a yellow alert in eight districts for 24 hours from 8:30 am on Oct 28 (IMD). Telangana's alerts are unchanged since the morning update.

cards.title: 🆕 Morning update (Oct 27): Telangana winds + rain till Nov 1
cards.body: IMD Hyderabad: heavy to very heavy rain likely Wed and Thu in Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam and Mahabubabad (Hans India). Gusty winds of 50–60 kmph likely in Bhupalapally, Mulugu, Kothagudem, Khammam, Suryapet, Mahabubabad, Warangal and Hanamkonda; 30–40 kmph elsewhere, Oct 27–30. Light to moderate rain statewide till Nov 1. Monday's IMD bulletin put Arnab 660 km ESE of Kakinada, moving west at 13 kmph.

cards.title: 🆕 Night update (Oct 26): landfall near Yanam–Kakinada
cards.body: Arnab is now a very severe cyclone, set to cross near Yanam–Kakinada (The Hindu). Andhra has a red alert in 7 districts: Kakinada, East Godavari, Konaseema, Eluru, West Godavari, Alluri Sitharama Raju, Anakapalli. Kakinada is evacuating 89,000 people; schools and colleges in the Godavari region get a two-day holiday; 67 Konaseema villages are moving to relief camps. The Centre reviewed preparedness and ordered zero loss of life (Times of India). Railways set up a 24x7 war room (Indian Express).

cards.title: 🆕 Evening update (Oct 26)
cards.body: Telangana's alerts start a day earlier: The Hindu reports orange alerts in four districts and yellow in four more on Oct 28, before the Oct 29 red alerts for Mulugu, Kothagudem, Khammam and Mahabubabad. Andhra has identified about 5.7 lakh people in vulnerable areas for evacuation (Hindustan Times). Railways cancelled 8 trains and rerouted 2 (Indian Express). Hyderabad: no rain alert yet.

cards.title: 🆕 Named: Cyclone Arnab (Oct 26)
cards.body: The storm is now Cyclone Arnab. Andhra's power utility APEPDCL has opened 41 control rooms and kept 4,056 workers ready; Kakinada, East Godavari and Konaseema residents can report outages on 1912. Odisha has banned fishing and tourist entry in 6 districts. Andhra's municipal polls are at risk; the State Election Commissioner expects normalcy within two days of landfall (The Hindu).

New IMD Hyderabad bulletin (via The Hans India, 26 Oct, 12:49 am). Oct 29 red alert (heavy to very heavy, isolated extremely heavy rain): Mulugu, Bhadradri Kothagudem, Khammam, Mahabubabad. Orange: Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Warangal, Suryapet, Nalgonda, Nagarkurnool. Gusty winds 50–60 kmph in 11 districts; 30–40 kmph in the rest, Hyderabad included.

cards.title: what changed (Oct 26, latest)
cards.body: 1) Red alert now named for Oct 29, and Mahabubabad joins the red list. 2) Nalgonda and Nagarkurnool move to orange. 3) Landfall window: between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, Oct 28 morning to early afternoon. 4) Bulletin position: 820 km ESE of Visakhapatnam, 1,010 km ESE of Machilipatnam. 5) Earlier (Oct 25): red for Mulugu, Kothagudem, Khammam on Oct 28.

Hyderabad city still has no IMD rain alert; expect gusty winds of 30–40 kmph and cooler days. An independent forecaster (via NewsMeter) sees minimums near 16°C in parts of Hyderabad. That's a private forecast, not IMD's.

data.hook: Rice that cost *₹45/kg* now sells for *₹90*. People are pre-booking harvests
data.hook_b: Rice at *₹90/kg*: are traders hoarding it?
data.tldr: Update Oct 27: traders in Telangana have been warned against creating an artificial rice shortage. Fine (sanna) rice that sold for about ₹45 a kg now costs over ₹90 in Telangana villages and Hyderabad. Families are paying farmers in advance to lock prices; farmers get ₹3,000–3,500 a quintal in open markets vs ₹2,450 MSP + ₹500 bonus.

beats.what: Open-market paddy prices jumped to ₹3,000–3,500 a quintal. Buyers are pre-booking harvests; one Vikarabad buyer paid ₹5,000 a quintal in advance.
beats.why: El Niño dried up water, the government is asking farmers not to sow rabi paddy, and people expect a shortage. CID also arrested 14 millers for diverting fine paddy and passing off coarse rice to FCI.
beats.care: Your monthly rice bill may double. Buying a bag now locks today's price, but you lose money if prices fall when the harvest peaks in December.

Farmers who struggled to sell at procurement centres last season now have buyers coming to them. Selling at the PPC means 10 days of drying from 35% to 17% moisture, so many sell wet paddy straight to the open market.

learn.t: MSP (minimum support price) is the floor the government pays for crops. When open-market prices beat MSP, less grain reaches the government's ration stock.

data.hook: 💥 Boom + *10-second* shake in Rajendranagar: NGRI says rain, not quake
data.hook_b: Felt the ground shake in Attapur at 10:25 am? Here's what it was
data.tldr: At about 10:25 am on Tuesday, a loud boom and 5–10 seconds of shaking sent residents of Rajendranagar, Attapur, Upparpally and Langar Houz into the streets. NGRI scientists blame 'hydro seismicity': rainwater building pressure in granite cracks. No deaths or major damage.

beats.what: A loud explosion-like sound, then 5–10 seconds of ground shaking across Hyderabad's south-western fringe.
beats.why: NGRI says it's hydro seismicity: water in granite fractures builds pressure and causes tiny underground ruptures. It's not a tectonic earthquake.
beats.care: Hyderabad sits on a stable granite shield, so a destructive quake is unlikely. If it happens again, step outside calmly and don't spread 'blast' rumours.

cards.title: What happened
cards.body: Tuesday, about 10:25 am. Rajendranagar, Upparpally, Attapur, Erraboda, Keshavswamy Nagar and Langar Houz heard a boom. The ground shook for 5–10 seconds. Windows rattled, utensils moved, people ran out. Officials urged calm; early checks found no deaths and no major structural damage (Siasat).

cards.title: Why the ground 'booms'
cards.body: Hyderabad's rock is old granite full of cracks. After heavy rain, water seeps in and pressure builds. When it releases, small ruptures underground make a loud bang and a short shake. Scientists call it hydro seismicity. It's local and shallow, unlike a real earthquake from moving plates.
It's happened before: Sulemannagar and Chintalmet in October 2020 and again in February 2026. A 1.8-magnitude micro-quake was recorded near Budvel in January 2015.

cards.q: Did you feel it?
What did NGRI say caused Tuesday's boom?
cards.why: Rainwater building pressure in granite fractures, per NGRI scientists (Siasat).

learn.t: Hydro seismicity: small, shallow tremors triggered when water seeps into rock fractures and changes the pressure inside them. It's why some quiet areas feel jolts after heavy rain.

HMWSSB is asking every household to cut water use by 20%. Easy wins: fix dripping taps, bucket over shower, reuse RO reject water for mopping.

cards.title: 🆕 Godavari water to the rescue (Oct 25)
cards.body: The Telangana government will divert Godavari water to areas that depend on the shrinking Singur and Manjira reservoirs, The Hindu reports. cards.title: 🚨 New: emergency declared (Oct 25)
cards.body: Hyderabad's water board has declared an emergency over the acute shortage, Siasat reports. Citing state irrigation department data (via ThePrint): over half of Telangana's 600-plus mandals are hit by drought, and only about 500 of the state's 6,000+ lakes still hold water. Watch for your area's supply schedule next.

Officials fear Singur could run dry within 60 days, by mid-December, and say drinking water needs can't be met from December. The water board is drawing up area-wise plans with an alternative source for each locality. A crop holiday has been declared in the Singur ayacut.

cards.title: Live in these areas? You're first in line

cards.title: Which areas are in the red zone?

Supply-wise, the western IT corridor (Gachibowli, HITEC City, Madhapur, Kondapur) leans on Singur, and the Old City on Osman Sagar.

Deputy CM Bhatti Vikramarka (Oct 24): peak power demand is now 20,018 MW (6,648 MW in 2014). Falling reservoirs cut hydropower, which normally gives ~3,500 MW at night peak. A Cabinet sub-committee is handling the crisis. Farmers with low groundwater are asked not to run motors.
HYDRAA found buildings in Borabanda and Navbharat Nagar pumping water straight out of Madhapur's Sunnam Cheruvu through dozens of hidden pipelines, with borewells drilled in bedrooms and kitchens.

data.hook: The Pacific just hit *30.06°C*, a record. That's the El Niño drying up Telangana
data.tldr: Sea temperatures in the Niño 3.4 zone crossed 30°C on Oct 5 for the first time on record, with the anomaly reaching 3.48°C on Oct 18. Scientists say El Niño has grown stronger over the last 40 years.

beats.what: On Oct 5, the Niño 3.4 region of the Pacific recorded 30.06°C, the first time on record. The temperature anomaly hit 3.48°C on Oct 18 and eased to 3.34°C this week.
beats.why: El Niño warms the Pacific and weakens India's monsoon. A Galápagos coral study led by Julia Cole (University of Michigan) found its strength has amplified over the last 40 years.
beats.care: This is why Telangana's rain is 17% short and Hyderabad's Singur dam is 11% full. Expect a tough summer for water and power.

cards.body: Scientists say the link between global warming and El Niño is still being researched, but the current event is 'well outside the norm' in the instrument record.

cards.q: Are you changing anything at home because of the water crisis?

cards.why: The first time it crossed 30°C on record.

viz.l: Niño 3.4 sea temperature, Oct 5: a record

learn.t: El Niño is when the central and eastern Pacific warm up. It shifts rain patterns worldwide and usually weakens India's monsoon.

beats.care: Blanket age bans on going online now face a high bar in India. Expect child modes, private-by-default accounts and stricter limits on strangers messaging teens.
beats.what: On 15 October, Justices Pardiwala and Vinod Chandran ruled that every child has a fundamental right to access and use the internet.
beats.why: The case was about platforms failing to remove child sexual abuse material. The court said punish the abusers and platforms, not the children.

cards.body: The court said keeping children offline would be to mistake the victim for the problem. It still allows targeted limits, like blocking adult sites, parental supervision and a dedicated child mode on social media.

Flagged abuse content must be checked by at least three trained human reviewers, matches to a known database removed at once, and reporting made possible in two steps. Big repeat offenders could face heavy fines.

cards.body: Nobody asked the court to declare an internet right. The plea, by an NGO, was about platforms not removing child abuse material since a 2024 ruling.
